content.text: Confirmed two correctness bugs. Posting the PR comment.

input.command:
gh pr comment 7 --repo Kenndal/trace-log-sec --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Review summary (critical / MVP-blocking only)

Overall this is a solid CLI MVP: clean Typer layout, good validation UX (aggregate errors), sensible config→CLI precedence, and solid test coverage. A few correctness issues are worth fixing before treating `analyze` as the real entrypoint.

### 1. Source IDs collide on basename (`cli/formats.py`)
`CombinedLogParser(source=path.stem)` / `SyslogAuthParser(source=path.stem)` means `host1/auth.log` and `host2/auth.log` both become source `"auth"`. That breaks:
- multi-source correlation (`≥2 sources` never fires across same-stem files)
- parse-error / evidence attribution (can't tell which file)

**Fix:** use something unique per path (e.g. `str(path)` or a disambiguated name).

### 2. Format sniff is first-line-only and fails closed
`detect_format` only tries the first non-blank line. A junk/header/rotation remnant at the top causes the whole file to be skipped (verified: `# rotated\n` + valid Combined line → skipped). For real logs this will silently drop input despite a warning.

**Fix:** sniff the first N non-blank lines (or first successful parse within a small window).

### 3. Auth-only runs anchor year to “now”
With no web logs, `_reference_time` falls back to `datetime.now(UTC)`. Archived auth logs then get the wrong year, which silently breaks threshold windows and correlation. Anchoring to web logs is good when present; auth-only historical analysis needs an explicit override (or at least a loud warning).

### 4. Web logs are fully parsed twice for year anchoring
`_reference_time` streams every detected web file end-to-end before `Engine.analyze` parses them again. Fine for fixtures; contradicts the “single-pass / memory-efficient” goal on large production logs. Prefer a cheap anchor (last parseable timestamp near EOF, file mtime, or CLI `--reference-time`).

---

Non-blocking for MVP: removing `strict`, the Typer registration pattern, and the config knobs all look fine. Happy to re-review after the source-ID / sniff fixes.
EOF
)"
input.description: Post critical review summary on PR

content.text:
PR looks solid as a CLI MVP; only a few **correctness** issues are worth blocking on.

### Critical

1. **Source ID collision** — `path.stem` makes `host1/auth.log` and `host2/auth.log` both `"auth"`, which breaks multi-source correlation and error attribution.
2. **First-line format sniff** — one junk header line skips the whole file (confirmed with `# rotated` + valid Combined content).
3. **Auth-only year anchoring** — no web logs → `datetime.now()`, so historical auth logs get the wrong year and threshold/correlation windows go wrong silently.
4. **Double-parse of web logs** — `_reference_time` fully reads every web file before `Engine.analyze` does it again; fine for fixtures, bad for large production logs.

Everything else (Typer layout, validation UX, config precedence, dropping `strict`) is fine for MVP.

Posted on the PR: https://github.com/Kenndal/trace-log-sec/pull/7#issuecomment-5139635192
